scope: Chrome Extensions APIs, Manifest V3 security/lifecycle guidance, and Chrome Web Store policies relevant to SiteWipe's reviewed permissions, destructive consent, local user-data handling, exact-report side-panel opening, and release claims
reviewMethod: All 29 first-party developer.chrome.com pages listed below were opened successfully on checkedAt and reconciled with the 1.11.38 manifest, runtime call sites, permission lifecycle, report binding, privacy wording, and remaining installed-evidence gaps. This ledger is not Chrome Web Store approval, legal advice, or installed-browser evidence.

localSourceContractValidation.evidenceBoundary: These are local source/static/Node-test results. They do not establish Chrome Web Store compliance, browser-native prompt behavior, incognito operation, MV3 suspension recovery, installed side-panel behavior, installed accessibility, performance, or exact packaged-byte behavior.

sources.title: Declare permissions
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Keep install-time authority narrow, explain warnings, declare optional host supersets in the manifest, and request only reviewed target subsets from a user gesture. Incognito still requires a separate user-controlled enablement on the extension details page.

sources.title: Permissions API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Optional host access must be requested inside a user gesture and may later be inspected or removed. SiteWipe inventories exact, broader, and all-site access separately, removes only independently proven temporary exact access, and preserves ambiguous grants for manual review.

sources.title: Extension service worker lifecycle
sources.siteWipeConclusion: MV3 workers can terminate and lose globals. SiteWipe uses validated session or durable state for approval, jobs, DNR recovery, temporary-access recovery, and startup safety, but installed termination/restart evidence remains required.

sources.title: Stay secure
sources.pageLastUpdated: reviewed on checkedAt; exact footer date not used as evidence
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Treat pages and messages as untrusted, minimize authority, keep logic packaged, use isolated execution, and validate inputs. SiteWipe applies local controls, but source design is not a platform certification.

sources.title: BrowsingData API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: The API can remove broad browser data. SiteWipe admits only explicit reviewed origins and allowlisted data types, rejects time/global deletion shapes, and documents browser-specific origin support.

sources.title: Cookies API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Cookie access depends on host permission and browser-exposed stores and partition keys. SiteWipe bounds discovery/removal, rematches targets, and treats missing partition visibility as uncertainty.

sources.title: Tabs API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: The tabs permission exposes sensitive metadata and mutation authority. SiteWipe reviews tab effects, re-reads each tab against target/private scope, and reports unresolved close outcomes as unknown.

sources.title: History API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: History exposes browsing activity. SiteWipe bounds searches, rematches every returned URL, deletes individual matching URLs only after authorization, and redacts retained results by default.

sources.title: Downloads API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Downloaded-file removal is irreversible. SiteWipe keeps it Expert-only and off by default, binds preflight IDs, and revalidates exact live identity/state/target immediately before removal. Detailed review requires the displayed typed phrase; explicitly enabled settings_direct truthfully skips that per-run phrase without weakening ID or live-record binding.

sources.title: Storage API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Extension storage is shared across extension contexts and survives worker globals. SiteWipe validates schemas, serializes mutations, limits approval lifetime, and applies reviewed privacy settings to report persistence.

sources.title: Scripting API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Injection requires scripting plus host authority or activeTab. SiteWipe injects packaged functions in the isolated world only after authorization and live target/private-scope checks; hostile-page installed evidence remains pending.

sources.title: Declarative Net Request API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: DNR rules can block requests. SiteWipe uses session rules only in a reserved ID range, persists recovery intent before mutation, clears the full owned range, and preserves uncertain timed-out recovery obligations.

sources.title: Side Panel API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Opening a side panel must occur in response to a user action. SiteWipe contracts a synchronous popup-gesture open in the exact verified window and an exact report/window binding before display. One exact-artifact installed opening is retained separately in browser-validation.json; focus, keyboard, zoom, replacement, and multi-window coverage remains incomplete.

sources.title: Alarms API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Alarms can wake an extension worker but are not durable wall-clock execution. SiteWipe treats them as bounded maintenance triggers and retains authoritative durable state.

sources.title: WebNavigation API
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Frame discovery expands navigation visibility. SiteWipe keeps webNavigation optional, Expert-only, off by default, and releases it when Standard mode is restored.

sources.title: Incognito manifest key
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Incognito access remains explicitly user-controlled and context-sensitive. SiteWipe binds private state into preflight and refuses durable private-scope report persistence; installed incognito evidence remains pending.

sources.title: Content Security Policy manifest key
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Extension-page CSP and MV3 packaging must prevent unsafe executable sources. SiteWipe uses packaged scripts and local static resources; scanners report no project-controlled remote code.

sources.title: Match patterns
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Host patterns are authority boundaries, not registrable-domain logic. SiteWipe derives canonical required patterns from its separately pinned PSL target model and does not accept arbitrary patterns from untrusted input.

sources.title: Quality guidelines
sources.siteWipeConclusion: A clear single purpose and stable user-facing functionality are required. SiteWipe is scoped to guarded site-specific browser cleanup; final installed behavior and listing evidence remain pending.

sources.title: Permissions policy
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Permissions must be necessary for current features and as narrow as practicable. SiteWipe has no required host patterns, requests exact optional target subsets, and documents its ten named permissions.

sources.title: User data FAQ
sources.pageLastUpdated: page footer reports 2016-04-23; content reviewed on checkedAt
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Local processing and storage of browsing activity still count as user-data handling and require disclosure and a privacy policy. Dashboard disclosures must match extension behavior and the stable hosted policy.

sources.title: Limited Use requirements
sources.siteWipeConclusion: User data must be limited to the disclosed single purpose and cannot be repurposed or transferred except under narrow conditions. SiteWipe states local-only use, but live dashboard and hosted-policy review remain action-time gates.

sources.title: Disclosure requirements
sources.siteWipeConclusion: User-data handling and destructive effects require clear, affirmative, informed disclosure. Detailed review is the default; settings-direct mode remains default-off, explicitly confirmed, completely preflight-bound, and truthfully reported.

sources.title: Manifest V3 requirements
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Extension logic must be self-contained and remote executable logic is prohibited. SiteWipe's explicit 55-file runtime closure and static scans enforce a local source boundary; exact artifact revalidation remains required.

sources.title: Minimum functionality
sources.siteWipeConclusion: The submitted artifact must work as described. Source tests and synthetic UI checks cannot replace installed exact-artifact validation.

sources.title: Unexpected behavior
sources.pageLastUpdated: reviewed on checkedAt; exact footer date not used as evidence
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Runtime behavior and disclosures must match reasonable expectations. Direct mode cannot conceal its lack of detailed review, and failures or unknown outcomes cannot be presented as successful cleanup.

sources.title: Listing requirements
sources.pageLastUpdated: reviewed on checkedAt; exact footer date not used as evidence
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Listing text and media must accurately represent the exact extension. Compatibility, accessibility, performance, privacy, deletion, identity, and release claims remain evidence-gated.

sources.title: Chrome Web Store listing fields
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Store metadata and media must be completed against the exact installed artifact and rechecked in the live dashboard at submission time.

sources.title: Troubleshooting Chrome Web Store violations
sources.pageLastUpdated: reviewed on checkedAt; exact footer date not used as evidence
sources.siteWipeConclusion: Review permission scope, privacy, deceptive behavior, metadata, and functionality against the exact submitted artifact. Local source readiness does not imply Store acceptance.

aiAssistanceDisclosureFinding.limitation: This is a dated technical review of the listed first-party pages, not a timeless legal or dashboard conclusion. Recheck official policy and every live submission field at action time.

siteWipeAssessment.singlePurpose: technically aligned with guarded, preflight-bound site-scoped cleanup; final listing and installed-behavior review pending
siteWipeAssessment.leastPrivilege: no required host patterns; exact optional target subsets; exact/broader/all-site pre-existing grant inventory; optional webNavigation is persisted off and released outside a later explicit Expert enable gesture; ten required named permissions have current feature rationales; native warning validation pending
siteWipeAssessment.destructiveConsent: fresh complete review remains the default in Standard and Expert; owner-approved settings_direct requires explicit saved confirmation, the same hidden complete preflight, one SiteWipe cleanup action, and truthful no-review reporting; native permission confirmation may be additional; installed interaction evidence pending
siteWipeAssessment.privateScope: immutable preflight-bound private authority and no durable missing private-target lease implemented; private-source direct mode requires Allow in incognito plus pre-existing exact target access; installed incognito lifecycle evidence pending
siteWipeAssessment.reportOpening: the 1.11.38 source contract synchronously opens the side panel from the popup gesture only after exact window/report prebinding and fails closed on stale binding; installed exact-artifact confirmation remains pending
siteWipeAssessment.userData: local processing is still user-data handling; reviewed privacy defaults and controls are documented; stable hosted policy and dashboard disclosure review remain pending
siteWipeAssessment.remoteCode: source scanners and the explicit 55-file runtime closure report no project-controlled remote code; exact final artifact revalidation remains required
siteWipeAssessment.browserEvidenceBoundary: ChatGPT in-app Browser synthetic UI evidence is not installed Chrome or Brave extension evidence
